title: Eat the frog is credited to Mark Twain. The advice to do your worst task first is usually attributed
description:
The advice to do your worst task first is usually attributed to him. Brian Tracy's book Eat That Frog! opens with that credit.

Quote Investigator found no substantive evidence, and the first known Twain link is a 1988 newspaper column. Twain died in 1910, 78 years earlier.

French writer. His collected works credit a toad a day to M. de Lassay.

The line was about swallowing a toad each morning so nothing in high society could disgust you later. It was a joke about society, not a task list.

The frog is a toad, and the author is French.

Sources:
- https://quoteinvestigator.com/2013/04/03/eat-frog/ (read): established that Quote Investigator found no substantive evidence Mark Twain said it, that the earliest known Twain link is a 1988 Cleveland Plain Dealer column, that the saying is traced to Nicolas Chamfort's works of about 1795 where it is credited to M. de Lassay and uses a toad, and that Brian Tracy's Eat That Frog! opens with the Twain attribution.
- https://wist.info/chamfort-nicolas/67155/ (read): established the French wording "Faudrait avaler un crapaud tous les matins" and the English "swallow a toad every morning", from Chamfort's Products of Perfected Civilization, 1795, credited to M. de Lassay, in the context of facing high society so as to meet nothing more disgusting during the day.
